children: MEXICO CITY--Mexico's inflation was mixed in August with increases in fresh food prices contributing to a higher overall rate while core inflation slowed.
The consumer price index rose 0.20% last month and was up 3.26% from a year-earlier, compared with an annual rate of 3.12% in July, national statistics institute Inegi said Wednesday.
Core CPI, which excludes energy and perishable food prices, rose 0.16% in August, pushing the 12-month rate down to 3.88% from 3.95% in July.

An increase in fresh food prices last month was partially offset by a decline in energy costs. Increases in college fees and some public transportation contributed to a rise in services, while airfares and vacation packages fell after the summer holiday season.
The Bank of Mexico, which kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 6.5% at its last two meetings, expects inflation to reach its 3% target in the fourth quarter of 2027.

title: Mexico's Inflation Picks Up in August, But Core Rate Slows
